medium_value.description: Change simple-release to explicitly allow only bugfix and other, and test an unknown or empty pr_type with a nonempty PR number.

Define unified-diff synthesis for files with and without a final newline, CRLF content, blank lines, and empty content. Include the no-final-newline marker where applicable and verify the generated hunk line count.
Specify how pre-retained synthesized patches merge with pass-2 results, preserve source metadata, and are discarded when the head-pin recheck triggers a restart. Add tests for these paths.
Escape filenames and matched patterns for the PR summary, including Markdown delimiters, HTML, and embedded line breaks, and test hostile display strings.
Define protected_kept as an exclusion-stage outcome and show each file's final reviewed or omitted status, or rename the rendered list to make that distinction explicit.

Validate the complete contents endpoint shape, including owner and repository segments, and define whether path validation occurs before or after percent encoding. Add tests for encoded traversal, encoded separators, empty segments, and option-like inputs.
Separate classifier unit tests from wrapper no-PR behavior and state precisely where a PR number is required for housekeeping output.
Replace textual guard matching with tests that evaluate the actual workflow conditions across the full type and PR-number matrix, including missing and unexpected outputs.

Specify that CPU guardrails measure synchronous work in an isolated test process, or account explicitly for unrelated concurrent activity and asynchronous execution. Define the workload and measurement procedure for the quadratic negative control.

Define the supported wildcard grammar and make the fallback implement the same semantics as the native matcher. Add differential tests for ?, character classes, braces, malformed patterns, and dot segments.
Handle exceptions from native glob evaluation and specify literal or no-match behavior for malformed patterns.

Resolve all matching user patterns before applying protection: an explicit non-wildcard match should exclude a protected file even when an earlier wildcard also matches. Specify which pattern is recorded and test both pattern orders.

Specify normalization at each pattern source, including how .reviewignore trailing slashes are preserved or converted before wildcard detection, and test equivalent entries through the actual configuration loaders.
Apply exclusions before content retrieval and introduce a cumulative retrieval byte budget, per-call timeout, and total retrieval deadline, with deterministic fallback when a bound is reached.

Budget the synthesized patch rather than only the source content, including added plus prefixes and the hunk header. Define whether an oversized synthesized patch is truncated through existing selection or rejected, and add boundary tests.
Require byte-preserving subprocess output for content retrieval, perform size and fatal UTF-8 validation on those bytes, and decode to a string only afterward.

Remove content-based detection of a JSON response envelope. Use a fixed response contract or an independently identified transport response format, and test a legitimate source file containing content and encoding keys.
If JSON-envelope support is retained, specify its encoded-response size bound, decoded-content size bound, strict envelope validation, and malformed-base64 behavior.

Change the simple-release guard from a negative list to a positive list (`pr_type == 'bugfix' || pr_type == 'other'`) && pr_number != '', or correct § 6 to say that an unexpected pr_type value WILL run simple-release. Add a bats case in post-merge-workflow-guards.bats that an unknown value (e.g. `pr_type=foo` with a PR number) skips both prepare jobs.

Define the synthesized-patch byte budget and line splitting precisely: fetch at most `maxDiffBytes − header − N` bytes or state that a synthesized patch may exceed `max_diff_bytes` by the `+`/header overhead and is still accepted; strip one trailing `\n` before splitting so N equals the real line count and no spurious empty `+` line is appended; state CRLF handling.

State in § 6 and C-3 that synthesized patches obtained during pass 1 are pinned to `pin.head_sha` and must be discarded when the post-pass-1 `recheck` detects a moved head and restarts; add a paged-fetch test for the restart path with a fetched file.

Specify that `getFileContent` is called with the BASE repository's owner/repo and the pinned head sha (not the fork's coordinates), and add a note/test for fork-sourced PRs; have `assertAllowedArgs` also reject empty and `.` path segments.

Either narrow `isWildcardPattern` to `/[*?]/` or specify and test `dotSegmentGlobMatch`'s support for `{a,b}` brace alternation and `[abc]` classes so the fallback matcher's behaviour for those characters is defined on Node 20.
Have `segmentMatch` strip a single leading `/` (gitignore root anchor) before matching, or document that leading-slash patterns are unsupported; add a test case for `/README.md`.
Remove Q-2 from § 10 (it is already decided by DEC-1013) and move the depth-agnostic default note to § 11.D or § 9; keep § 10 to genuinely open items (Q-1, Q-3).

Assign the FR-2 test 'the rendered summary lists protected-kept files' to B's `paged-fetch.test.ts` (B owns rendering) rather than A's `loa-detection.test.ts`/`truncation.test.ts`, and list it in the FR-2 row accordingly.

Define the rendering when a protected-kept file is subsequently omitted or truncated by the size/file budget (it would appear in both `protected_kept` and `omitted`); e.g. annotate the protected entry with 'then omitted (budget)' or exclude it from the kept list.

Note in C-5 that `process.cpuUsage()` includes parallel GC helper threads and JIT compilation, so measured CPU time can exceed wall time for allocation-heavy code; either take the minimum of N (e.g. 3) runs or raise the 100 ms bound by a stated margin, and record the chosen rule in the assertion message.

Ensure Loa-tier omissions in the coverage record and PR summary carry the matching default pattern, so a depth-agnostic match such as `docs/PROCESS.md` ← `PROCESS.md` is visible to the operator; add it to § 4 and the FR-1 tests.

Decide the fate of the `.reviewignore` `/` → `**` conversion at truncation.ts:395 and state it in C-1/C-2. Either remove the conversion (the new segmentMatch already handles a trailing `/` directory pattern) or define explicitly whether a directory pattern that was rewritten to `dir/**` counts as a wildcard for the protected-paths rule. Add a test: `.github/workflows/` in `.reviewignore` vs the same string in `exclude_patterns` must yield the same excluded/protectedKept result.

Decide now whether the orchestrator `--type housekeeping` pin lives in `post-merge-publication.bats` or a new `post-merge-orchestrator-type.bats`; if new, add it to the § 7 landing suite list, C's allowlist by name, and the CI mirror invocation.

Assign documentation of the `(source: contents)` coverage marker and the patch-less-file fetch behaviour in SKILL.md to an implementer (B, with the SKILL.md section added to B's allowlist, or the lead), since A's SKILL.md ownership is limited to the exclusion/protected-paths text.

Make `dotSegmentGlobMatch` the authoritative wildcard matcher and drop `path.matchesGlob` from the production path (keep it only as a cross-check inside tests), or define `native` as authoritative-when-present with the fallback used only when absent. Do not OR the two results.

Replace 'kept when the first matching user pattern is a wildcard' with an order-independent rule: a file is kept iff it matches a protected pattern AND no non-wildcard user pattern matches it; record the first matching wildcard pattern in `protectedKept[].pattern`. Add a test with `['**/*.yml', '.github/workflows/ci.yml']` in both orders.

Apply the Loa-tier and user exclusion matchers (with protection) to the candidate list BEFORE issuing pass-1 content fetches, so excluded files are never fetched. Introduce a dedicated cap (e.g. `max_content_fetches`, default well below `maxFilesPerPr`) and an overall time budget for the fetch loop; record the count of fetches attempted in the coverage record.

Size `maxBuffer` for the base64-JSON fallback shape (≈ maxBytes × 4/3 + JSON overhead), not `maxBytes + 1024`; map an execFile `maxBuffer exceeded` error explicitly to `{ kind: 'too_large' }`; correct the § 9 row that says the contents endpoint caps raw responses at 1 MiB (the raw media type serves files up to 100 MB, so the size bound must be enforced client-side). Add the oversize case to the FR-3 test row for both response shapes.

Specify how `truncateFiles` receives `protectedPatterns` (new parameter vs. existing options/config object) and put that signature or options-type change into the lead's contract commit (D-2.1). Name which implementer edits the `truncateFiles` call site(s) in paged-fetch.ts if the signature changes.

Either declare `getFileContent` optional on `IGitProvider` (`getFileContent?:`, absent → no fetch, today's behaviour) or add the port method to the contract commit and enumerate every in-tree implementer and test double of `IGitProvider` that must gain the method, assigning each to an allowlist.

Extend the coverage record so a file that stayed `no_patch` after a content fetch was attempted carries the outcome (`fetch: 'binary' | 'too_large' | 'error' | 'skipped_cap'`), and render it in the omissions list. Add this to the § 3 record shape and the FR-3 tests.

Add a configuration key (e.g. `bridgebuilder.fetch_missing_patches: boolean`, default true) that disables the pass-1 content fetch, documented alongside `protected_paths` in SKILL.md, and a test that `false` leaves patch-less files at today's `no_patch` with no provider call.

blockers.concern: Combining native glob matching with a fallback using OR does not guarantee identical results when native matching is unavailable.
blockers.why_matters: Any pattern accepted only by the native implementation changes which files receive review across supported Node versions. The specified parity tests cover only a subset of wildcard syntax.
blockers.recommendation: Define one supported glob grammar and implement identical semantics in both paths. Add differential tests covering braces, character classes, escaping, malformed patterns, and native-only constructs.

blockers.concern: Protection is order-dependent: C-2 keeps a file when 'the first matching user pattern is a wildcard'. If the operator lists `**/*.yml` before `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the exact pattern never wins, which contradicts § 5.2 ('a non-wildcard user pattern that names a protected file excludes it').
blockers.why_matters: The operator's explicit intent is silently overridden depending on list order, and the recorded `pattern` on the protectedKept entry will name the wildcard, hiding the fact that an exact exclusion existed. Behaviour becomes unpredictable across `--exclude`, `exclude_patterns` and `.reviewignore` concatenation order.
blockers.recommendation: Define: a protected file is excluded iff at least one non-wildcard user pattern matches it; otherwise, if any wildcard matches, it is kept. Make the rule independent of order; add red tests for both orders and for the three sources being concatenated.

blockers.concern: The raw-response fallback identifies metadata JSON by inspecting file contents rather than an unambiguous response contract.
blockers.why_matters: A legitimate added JSON file containing content and encoding fields could be decoded as an API envelope, causing the reviewer to inspect different bytes from the committed file.
blockers.recommendation: Choose one explicit response format or distinguish formats through response metadata. Test a raw JSON source file that resembles a GitHub contents response.

blockers.concern: The simple-release guard accepts unexpected classifier values, contrary to the stated error-handling behavior.
blockers.why_matters: Any nonempty PR number combined with an unknown type passes both negative comparisons and can trigger release preparation.
blockers.recommendation: Use an explicit allowlist for bugfix and other, and test unknown, empty, and malformed classifier outputs.

blockers.concern: The trust boundary of `.reviewignore` is unstated. § 1.3 reads it from `repoRoot`, and § 1.2 asserts selection is a function of 'the operator's configuration', but if the review runs on a checkout of the PR head (or the pull_request merge commit), the PR author controls `.reviewignore`. By design (§ 5.2) a non-wildcard pattern that names a protected file excludes it, so a PR that adds the line `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or just `.github`) to `.reviewignore` removes the workflow from review, and `.reviewignore` itself is not in DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS.
blockers.why_matters: If the assumption is wrong, the protected-paths feature (FR-2) is bypassable with a one-line change in the same PR, and the exact threat it exists to mitigate (CI workflow / hook changes slipping past review) remains open while the coverage record reports everything as fine.
blockers.recommendation: State where `.reviewignore` is read from. Read it from the base ref (or another trusted ref), never from the PR head; add `.reviewignore` to DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS; when the PR modifies `.reviewignore`, apply the base version and record 'reviewignore changed in PR' in the coverage record. Add a test: PR modifies `.reviewignore` to exclude a workflow → workflow still reviewed.
